knowledge:
- key_parameters: tfile=The first argument of callpeak, representing the treatment alignment file (e.g., BED, BAM) ;; cfile=The second argument of callpeak, representing the control/input alignment file ;; gsize=Effective genome size (e.g., 5.2e7) ;; store_bdg=Logical, whether to store bedGraph files for treatment pileup and control lambda ;; name=Prefix name for output files ;; outdir=Directory where output files will be written ;; cutoff_analysis=Logical, whether to perform cutoff vs peak number/length analysis ;; broad=Logical, whether to call broad peaks instead of narrow peaks
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing ChIP-seq (or other DNA enrichment assays like ATAC-seq) data to identify significant regions of read enrichment (peaks) over a random background, using treatment and optionally control alignment files.
- pitfalls: The package relies on basilisk to automatically install and manage a Python conda environment with macs3. Users must ensure their system supports Python/Conda environments via basilisk and have write permissions for the cache directory where the virtual environment is created.

workflows.name: narrow_and_broad_peak_calling
workflows.intent: Call narrow and broad peaks from ChIP-seq treatment and control alignment files.
input: CHIP (treatment alignment file in BED or BAM format)
CTRL (control alignment file in BED or BAM format)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the MACSr package ;; 2. Retrieve test data from ExperimentHub ;; 3. Call narrow peaks using callpeak with cutoff analysis ;; 4. Call broad peaks using callpeak with broad=TRUE ;; 5. Inspect the resulting macsList objects, including arguments, outputs, and logs.
workflows.code:
library(MACSr)
eh <- ExperimentHub::ExperimentHub()
eh <- AnnotationHub::query(eh, "MACSdata")
CHIP <- eh[["EH4558"]]
CTRL <- eh[["EH4563"]]
cp1 <- callpeak(CHIP, CTRL, gsize = 5.2e7, store_bdg = TRUE,
                name = "run_callpeak_narrow0", outdir = tempdir(),
                cutoff_analysis = TRUE)
cp2 <- callpeak(CHIP, CTRL, gsize = 5.2e7, store_bdg = TRUE,
                name = "run_callpeak_broad", outdir = tempdir(),
                broad = TRUE)
cp1
cp2
cp1$arguments
cp1$outputs
cat(paste(cp1$log, collapse="\n"))
